item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is inviting qualified professionals to apply for four home-based consultancy opportunities supporting global and regional work in communications, gender-based violence prevention, harmful practices, female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C), research, advocacy and accountability.

The opportunities are designed for professionals with relevant academic qualifications and practical experience who can contribute to UNFPA programmes remotely. The assignments cover areas ranging from internal communications and technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) to research on harmful practices and evidence-based advocacy on FGM/C.

The four opportunities have different requirements, durations and application deadlines, so interested applicants should carefully review the specific Terms of Reference before applying.

UNFPA Home-Based Consultancy Opportunities 2026

The available positions are:

  1. Internal Communications Consultant
  2. Consultant Expert on TFGBV Capacity Strengthening of Frontline Service
  3. Consultant to Document Successful Programming Approaches on Addressing Harmful Practices
  4. Consultant on FGM Evidence-Based Advocacy and Accountability

All four positions are home-based, although the nature of individual assignments and operational requirements may differ.

1. Internal Communications Consultant

The Internal Communications Consultant will support UNFPA’s internal communications and stakeholder engagement activities under the Media and Communications Branch of the Division of External Relations.

The consultant will contribute to the implementation of the UNFPA global communications strategy and produce communications materials for internal audiences.

Key Details

  • Location: Home-based
  • Contract type: Consultancy
  • Duration: Six months, with possibility of extension
  • Level: Consultant
  • Category: Communications
  • Deadline: 4 September 2026 at 17:00

Key Responsibilities

The successful consultant will be expected to:

  • Write, edit and publish text and multimedia content.
  • Produce feature articles and interviews for internal platforms, newsletters, communications hubs and the Voices newsmagazine.
  • Support the organization of the General Staff Meeting, including communications, logistics and reporting.
  • Manage and present analytics relating to internal communication channels such as the intranet and newsletters.
  • Help organize training sessions, webinars and other internal communication events.
  • Develop resource materials for staff training.
  • Conduct research and generate ideas relating to internal and corporate communications.
  • Support the coordination and production of in-person events and exhibitions.
  • Undertake other relevant assignments from the Media and Communications Branch.

Education Requirements

Candidates must:

  • Have recently graduated from a master’s degree or higher.
  • Hold an undergraduate university degree.

Experience and Skills

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Some relevant work experience.
  • At least one year of relevant professional experience in communications, marketing or public relations is an advantage.
  • Excellent writing and editing skills.
  • Strong organizational and research skills.
  • Knowledge of web production, social media and multimedia tools.
  • Strong interpersonal communication and project management skills.
  • Experience working with development agencies, including in a volunteer capacity, is useful.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Fluency in English. Knowledge of other languages is an asset.

How to Apply

Applicants should submit their resume and cover letter by email to voices@unfpa.org by 4 September 2026. The source provides the official UNFPA Terms of Reference for the position.

2. Consultant Expert on TFGBV Capacity Strengthening

UNFPA’s Asia and the Pacific Regional Office is seeking a consultant to strengthen programming addressing technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) across the region.

The assignment focuses on prevention and survivor-centred responses, including strengthening frontline service providers, developing guidance and tools, training, stakeholder engagement and digital response mechanisms.

Key Details

  • Location: Home-based
  • Contract type: Temporary Appointment
  • Duration: Up to 100 working days between September 2026 and the end of March 2027
  • Job ID: 36614
  • Level: Consultant
  • Deadline: 8 September 2026 at 23:59

Key Responsibilities

The consultant will contribute to:

  • Developing tools, standard operating procedures and guidelines for frontline responders.
  • Strengthening survivor-centred TFGBV response services.
  • Supporting secure referral pathways and confidential case intake.
  • Supporting ethical collection and management of sensitive data.
  • Facilitating knowledge sharing among relevant stakeholders.
  • Documenting lessons learned and emerging trends.
  • Developing culturally appropriate TFGBV prevention materials.
  • Facilitating consultations with governments, UN agencies, development partners and civil society.
  • Reviewing laws and policies relating to TFGBV.
  • Facilitating Training of Trainers programmes on online harm and digital security.
  • Adapting and rolling out TFGBV guidance and training resources.
  • Supporting the TFGBV Response Hub and survivor-centred rapid-response mechanisms.

Expected Deliverables

Among the expected outputs are:

  • At least three tools, SOPs and guidelines for frontline responders.
  • Knowledge-sharing webinar reports.
  • A strategic brief documenting lessons and emerging trends.
  • Technical reviews of at least three laws and policies.
  • At least two culturally appropriate TFGBV prevention knowledge products.
  • Stakeholder consultation reports.
  • Contextualized TFGBV guidance and training resources.
  • A Training of Trainers report.
  • Reports supporting the TFGBV Response Hub and survivor-centred rapid-response system.

Qualifications and Experience

Candidates should have:

  • A master’s degree in public administration, health, social work, political science, gender studies, human rights and AI policy, technology or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant professional experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in GBV, SRHR and/or TFGBV programming.
  • Experience in content development and/or training design.
  • Strong understanding of GBV guiding principles and survivor-centred responses.
  • Experience providing remote or digital support to survivors of online violence.
  • Experience with digital support services, online helplines or digital response mechanisms is desirable.
  • Research or situational-analysis experience.
  • Experience developing and delivering culturally appropriate training.
  • Experience facilitating workshops and webinars.
  • Knowledge of safety by design, confidentiality and personal data protection.

Experience working with civil society, women-led organizations, community networks and frontline actors is also relevant. UN system experience is an advantage, while fluency in written and spoken English is required.

How to Apply

Applicants should review the full Terms of Reference and submit their application through the UNFPA vacancy for Job ID 36614.

3. Consultant to Document Successful Programming Approaches on Addressing Harmful Practices

This consultancy is focused on researching, analysing and documenting approaches to addressing harmful practices, particularly child marriage and female genital mutilation (FGM).

UNFPA’s Asia-Pacific Regional Office is seeking an experienced consultant to synthesize evidence on social norms change and develop strategic knowledge products and advocacy briefs highlighting successful programming approaches, impacts and lessons learned.

Key Details

  • Location: Home-based
  • Contract type: Temporary Appointment
  • Duration: Up to 155 working days, from 1 November 2026 to 30 October 2027
  • Job ID: 36609
  • Level: Consultant
  • Deadline: 6 September 2026 at 23:59

Key Areas of Work

The consultant will contribute to seven planned knowledge products covering areas such as:

  • TUSIP Catalytic Impact and funding pathways.
  • Adaptive management and programme responses during crises.
  • Long-term investment and social norm change.
  • Evidence-based approaches to ending FGM in Indonesia.
  • UNFPA’s comparative advantage and collaborative strengths.
  • Drivers and strategic interventions addressing child, early and forced marriage.
  • Pronatalism and child, early and forced marriage.

The consultant will also support at least four countries in the region in measuring social norms change through the development and rollout of a harmonized measurement tool.

Expected Deliverables

Expected outputs include:

  • Inception report and analytical framework.
  • Stakeholder mapping.
  • Draft outlines for knowledge products.
  • First drafts of knowledge products.
  • Finalized knowledge products.
  • Validation workshop materials and report.
  • Social norms change measurement tool.
  • Report summarizing country accompaniment.

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should have:

  • An advanced degree, such as a PhD or master’s, in gender studies, sociology, human rights, public health or international development.
  • At least 10 years of relevant research and programming experience addressing harmful practices and changing social norms.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting research or documenting programmes on social norms change, harmful practices or GBV.
  • Experience with UNFPA or UNICEF programming addressing harmful practices.
  • Expert-level ability to write policy briefs and strategic documents for high-level institutional donors.
  • Strong writing and documentation skills.
  • Proficiency in English.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should review the official UNFPA Terms of Reference and apply through the vacancy for Job ID 36609.

4. Consultant on FGM Evidence-Based Advocacy and Accountability

UNFPA is also seeking an international consultant to support evidence-based advocacy and accountability efforts relating to female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) in the Asia-Pacific region.

The consultant will translate research findings, empirical data and legal and policy analysis into advocacy messages, policy briefs and movement-building initiatives.

Key Details

  • Location: Home-based
  • Contract type: Temporary Appointment
  • Duration: 80 working days, from 28 September 2026 to 15 June 2027
  • Job ID: 36564
  • Level: Consultant
  • Deadline: 1 September 2026 at 23:59, America/New_York
  • Travel: No travel is expected

Key Responsibilities

The consultant will:

  • Map civil society organizations working on FGM/C across the region.
  • Support geo-visualization of the mapping.
  • Support implementation of the Regional FGM Accountability Framework.
  • Develop tools and tracking mechanisms for regional coalitions.
  • Monitor institutional commitments, human rights reporting and legal compliance.
  • Coordinate strategic dialogues, webinars and peer-learning workshops.
  • Synthesize regional research, national datasets and thematic studies.
  • Examine issues including medicalization, social norms and legal barriers.
  • Draft evidence-based advocacy briefs, technical notes and policy messages.
  • Support advocacy events and regional platforms.
  • Strengthen knowledge management, cross-country learning and movement building.

Expected Deliverables

The assignment includes deliverables such as:

  • Regional CSO mapping.
  • Tools and tracking mechanisms for monitoring commitments and legal compliance.
  • Advocacy materials and strategic session reports.
  • Synthesis of regional FGM/C research and datasets.
  • Geo-visualization of the regional mapping.
  • Implementation guide for the Regional Accountability Framework.
  • Strategic dialogues, webinars and peer-learning opportunities.
  • Evidence-based advocacy briefs, technical notes and policy messages.

Qualifications and Experience

Candidates should have:

  • An advanced university degree in public health, human rights, international relations, gender studies, social sciences or a related field.
  • Experience in research synthesis and drafting policy briefs, factsheets or technical reports.
  • Experience in research or advocacy relating to FGM, GBV or harmful practices is desirable.
  • Experience coordinating meetings, workshops, networks or multi-stakeholder consultations.
  • Knowledge or exposure to FGM/C, harmful practices or social norm change in the Asia-Pacific region is a strong asset.
  • Experience with UN system operations, gender programming or DFAT-funded projects is desirable.
  • Previous UNFPA experience is an asset.
  • Strong English drafting and communication skills.
  • Excellent time management, file organization and task-tracking skills.

How to Apply

Applicants should review the full Terms of Reference and apply through the official UNFPA vacancy for Job ID 36564.

Important Information for Applicants

These are professional consultancy assignments, and applicants should not assume that all four positions have the same eligibility requirements. Each vacancy has its own academic, professional and technical criteria.

Candidates should therefore:

  1. Identify the consultancy that best matches their qualifications and experience.
  2. Read the complete Terms of Reference.
  3. Check the specific closing date and time.
  4. Prepare a CV/resume that clearly demonstrates relevant experience.
  5. Prepare a tailored cover letter or other documents requested in the individual vacancy.
  6. Ensure that all required application materials are submitted before the relevant deadline.

Applicants should also note that consultants are responsible for having medical insurance for the duration of the consultancy; UNFPA does not provide medical insurance for consultants.

UNFPA also states that it does not charge application, processing, training, interview, testing or recruitment fees. Applicants should be cautious of anyone requesting payment or financial information in connection with these opportunities.

Conclusion

These four UNFPA home-based consultancy opportunities provide professionals with the opportunity to contribute to international development work in communications, gender-based violence prevention, harmful practices, FGM/C advocacy, research and accountability.

The positions vary considerably in terms of academic qualifications, professional experience, assignment duration and deadlines. Applicants should focus on the vacancy that most closely matches their background and carefully follow the official application instructions.

Apply early and review the complete Terms of Reference before submitting your application.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The World Health Organization (WHO) is recruiting a Research Officer (P2) to support work on neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) through the Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases (ESPEN).

  • Location: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso
  • Position: Research Officer
  • Grade: P2
  • Contract: 12 months
  • Deadline: 11 September 2026 at 2:59 PM
  • Starting annual base salary: USD 56,046, plus applicable post adjustment and other benefits

About the Position

The Research Officer will work under the direction of the ESPEN Team Leader and direct supervision of the ESPEN Laboratory Head.

The role contributes to WHO’s work to reduce the morbidity, mortality and disability associated with neglected tropical diseases, with particular attention to diseases amenable to preventive chemotherapy. These include lymphatic filariasis, onchocerciasis, soil-transmitted helminthiasis, schistosomiasis and trachoma.

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will contribute to laboratory research, surveillance, GIS and capacity-building activities.

Key duties include:

  • Contributing to the development of laboratory protocols, standard operating procedures and diagnostic tools for NTDs.
  • Providing technical support for operational research related to NTD elimination.
  • Conducting O-150 PCR entomological testing of S. damnosum s.l. adults using molecular biology techniques.
  • Conducting entomological analyses.
  • Documenting and disseminating laboratory best practices and protocols.
  • Supporting collaborative operational research activities and scientific publications.
  • Maintaining laboratory databases.
  • Developing mapping of laboratory data and entomological surveillance results.
  • Working with the ESPEN data team in Brazzaville.
  • Supporting inter-country and national training activities to build laboratory and field research capacity.

Required Qualifications

Education

Applicants must have a first university degree in one of the following fields:

  • Computer Sciences
  • Information System Engineering
  • Geographical Information System (GIS)
  • Public Health
  • Parasitology
  • Medical Entomology

Advanced certification or additional qualifications in areas such as computer sciences, molecular biology, parasitology, entomology, laboratory sciences or related fields are desirable.

Professional Experience

Applicants must have a minimum of two years of national and international experience in areas including:

  • Applied molecular biology
  • Research and development of surveillance tools for onchocerciasis or other priority NTDs in Africa
  • GIS data transformation
  • Mapping and spatial modelling of onchocerciasis foci

Previous experience with WHO and a strong publication record on onchocerciasis or other NTDs are considered desirable.

Required Skills

The position requires strong technical knowledge and research capabilities.

Applicants should have:

  • Excellent knowledge of the epidemiology of onchocerciasis.
  • Knowledge of onchocerciasis transmission, distribution and socioeconomic impact.
  • Knowledge of disease control and elimination strategies in the African Region.
  • Knowledge of lymphatic filariasis epidemiology and control strategies.
  • Strong GIS and remote-sensing skills.
  • Ability to analyse biological specimens involving vectors and parasites.
  • Ability to conduct laboratory needs assessments.
  • Ability to coordinate training activities in NTD field research, GIS and mapping.

Language Requirements

Essential: Expert knowledge of French.

Desirable: Intermediate knowledge of English.

The language requirements are interchangeable according to the vacancy information.

Salary and Benefits

The position is classified at P2 level.

The annual base salary starts at USD 56,046, subject to applicable mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance.

The position also includes a variable post adjustment, currently stated as USD 1,789 per month for the Ouagadougou duty station.

Other benefits include:

  • 30 days of annual leave
  • Allowances for dependent family members
  • Home leave
  • Education grant for dependent children

WHO Competencies

The vacancy identifies the following core competencies:

  • Teamwork
  • Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
  • Communication
  • Producing results

Contract Duration

The Research Officer position is offered as a temporary appointment for 12 months.

The position is based in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and is a full-time role.

Additional Information

WHO notes that a written test and/or asynchronous video assessment may be used during the screening process.

Candidates who are retained for an interview will be required to provide scanned copies of the degrees, diplomas or certificates required for the position.

WHO also notes that educational qualifications must come from institutions accredited or recognised in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), subject to the stated exceptions and review procedures.

WHO encourages applications from women, persons with disabilities, and nationals of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

11 September 2026 at 2:59 PM

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for professionals with backgrounds in public health, parasitology, medical entomology, molecular biology, GIS, remote sensing, epidemiology and NTD research.

The strongest candidates will combine relevant academic training with at least two years of professional experience in NTD research, surveillance, molecular biology or GIS-based disease mapping.

Conclusion

The WHO Research Officer position in Ouagadougou provides an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute to regional efforts to control and eliminate neglected tropical diseases in Africa.

The role combines molecular biology, entomological surveillance, GIS, operational research, laboratory systems and capacity building, making it particularly relevant to professionals working at the intersection of public health, disease surveillance and scientific research.

Eligible candidates with the required academic background, professional experience and French-language proficiency should consider applying before 11 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Europe Defence and Security Fellowship 2027, hosted by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom in Shrivenham, offers a specialised opportunity for experienced professionals working in defence, security, government, law enforcement, intelligence, resilience, civil protection, and related international organisations.

Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and delivered by Cranfield University, the six-week fellowship is designed to strengthen the leadership, strategic decision-making, organisational resilience, cyber resilience, and emerging-technology capabilities of mid-career professionals from across Europe.

The programme brings together professionals who have demonstrated leadership potential and who have the ability to influence policy, strategy, organisational capability, or operational effectiveness within their organisations and countries.

Europe Defence and Security Fellowship 2027 at a Glance

  • Programme: Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship
  • Host institution: Cranfield University
  • Host location: Defence Academy of the United Kingdom, Shrivenham
  • Funding: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)
  • Duration: Six weeks
  • Cohort 1: 25 January – 5 March 2027
  • Cohort 2: 15 March – 23 April 2027
  • Application deadline: 27 September 2026 at 11:00 UTC
  • Target applicants: Mid-career European professionals in defence, security, government, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, and international organisations
  • Programme format: Teaching, discussions, practical exercises, site visits, individual research, simulations, workshops, and collaborative learning

About the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship

The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is designed for professionals who operate in environments where security and defence challenges are becoming increasingly complex and interconnected.

Modern security challenges can involve traditional defence concerns alongside cyber threats, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, organisational vulnerabilities, governance challenges, and international cooperation.

The fellowship therefore takes an interdisciplinary and applied approach.

Rather than focusing on a single area of defence or security, participants will explore how leadership, organisational culture, governance, technology, resilience, and strategic decision-making interact.

The programme is intended to help fellows become more effective leaders who can operate within rapidly changing security and defence environments.

Participants will engage in:

  • Teaching and academic learning
  • Group discussions
  • Practical exercises
  • Workshops
  • Simulations
  • Practitioner-led sessions
  • Site and institutional visits in the United Kingdom
  • Individual research
  • Collaborative learning
  • International professional networking

A major component of the fellowship will be the opportunity to develop a research project addressing a relevant policy, leadership, organisational, or security challenge.

What Is the Aim of the Fellowship?

The programme aims to develop professionals who can operate effectively in complex security and defence environments.

Through the fellowship, participants will strengthen their ability to understand and respond to challenges affecting:

  • Governments
  • International organisations
  • Public institutions
  • Defence organisations
  • Security institutions
  • Civil protection systems
  • Resilience structures

The programme places particular emphasis on practical leadership and strategic thinking.

Fellows will be encouraged to examine problems from different perspectives and consider how decisions made under uncertainty can affect organisations, governments, and societies.

Six-Week Fellowship Programme

The fellowship lasts for six weeks and is offered through two cohorts in 2027.

Cohort 1

25 January – 5 March 2027

Cohort 2

15 March – 23 April 2027

Applicants should therefore consider which cohort best fits their professional circumstances when applying.

Key Learning Areas of the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship

The programme is organised around six integrated themes.

1. Global Leadership in an Era of Complexity

The first theme focuses on leadership within an increasingly complex international environment.

Security and defence professionals frequently need to make decisions while dealing with multiple stakeholders, competing interests, uncertainty, and rapidly changing circumstances.

Through this theme, fellows will examine leadership challenges and consider approaches for operating effectively in complex environments.

2. Understanding People, Culture, and Organisations

Security and defence organisations are influenced not only by policies and structures but also by people, organisational culture, behaviour, and governance.

This theme examines how these factors can influence:

  • Institutional effectiveness
  • Organisational resilience
  • Vulnerability
  • Decision-making
  • Leadership
  • Organisational performance

Understanding organisational culture and human behaviour can help leaders identify both strengths and vulnerabilities within their institutions.

3. Cyber Resilience and Information Threats

Cybersecurity and information threats are increasingly important components of national and international security.

The fellowship will provide fellows with an opportunity to explore cyber resilience and understand the challenges associated with information threats.

Participants will consider how organisations can better understand and respond to emerging cyber-related risks.

This theme is particularly relevant to professionals whose responsibilities involve security policy, resilience, defence, intelligence, technology, or organisational risk.

4. Artificial Intelligence, Governance, and Emerging Technology

Artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are changing the way organisations operate and make decisions.

At the same time, these technologies create new governance, security, and ethical challenges.

The fellowship will examine both the opportunities and risks associated with artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies.

Participants will be encouraged to consider how governments and organisations can respond to technological change while maintaining effective governance and resilience.

5. Strategic Decision-Making Under Pressure

Security and defence professionals may be required to make important decisions in circumstances characterised by:

  • Uncertainty
  • Incomplete information
  • Competing pressures
  • Rapidly changing conditions

The fellowship will explore strategic decision-making approaches that can help professionals respond effectively in such environments.

The focus is not simply on making decisions, but on understanding the conditions under which strategic decisions are made and the factors that can influence their effectiveness.

6. Building Resilience and Future Leadership

The final theme brings together the fellowship’s emphasis on resilience and leadership.

Participants will explore how organisations can prepare for future challenges while developing leaders who can operate effectively in changing environments.

This theme connects leadership development with organisational resilience and the ability to anticipate and respond to future security challenges.

What Will Fellows Do During the Programme?

The Europe Defence and Security Fellowship uses a variety of learning methods rather than relying exclusively on classroom teaching.

Participants will have opportunities to engage in:

Lectures

Fellows will receive structured academic and professional input covering the programme’s major themes.

Workshops

Workshops will provide opportunities to explore issues in greater depth and apply concepts to practical situations.

Simulations

Practical simulations will allow fellows to engage with scenarios that reflect complex decision-making environments.

Practitioner Speakers

Fellows will hear from practitioners and professionals with relevant experience in defence, security, leadership, policy, and related areas.

Research Activity

Each fellow will work on an individual research project addressing a relevant challenge.

UK Institutional Visits

The programme includes visits to relevant institutions in the United Kingdom, providing participants with additional opportunities to understand institutional practices.

Collaborative Learning

Participants will learn alongside professionals from different European countries and professional backgrounds, creating opportunities for the exchange of ideas and experiences.

Fellowship Research Project

A significant component of the programme is the individual research project.

Throughout the fellowship, participants will work on a research project addressing a relevant:

  • Policy challenge
  • Leadership challenge
  • Organisational challenge
  • Security challenge

Fellows will receive academic support while developing their research.

At the conclusion of the programme, participants will have the opportunity to present their findings to the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) in London.

This gives fellows an opportunity to connect their research to real-world policy and institutional challenges.

International Networking Opportunities

Another important aspect of the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is professional networking.

The programme brings together professionals from across Europe and the UK, creating opportunities to establish relationships across:

  • Countries
  • Professional sectors
  • Government institutions
  • Security organisations
  • Defence communities
  • International organisations

The fellowship is designed to create enduring professional networks that can continue beyond the six-week programme.

For professionals working in security and defence, these international relationships can be valuable for exchanging knowledge, experiences, and perspectives on shared challenges.

Who Can Apply for the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship?

The fellowship is specifically intended for mid-career professionals from eligible European countries who demonstrate leadership potential in security and defence.

Applicants must meet the programme’s additional eligibility requirements as well as the standard Chevening eligibility criteria.

Citizenship and Residency Requirement

At the point of application, applicants must be citizens of and residents in one of the following countries:

  • Andorra
  • Austria
  • Belgium
  • Bulgaria
  • Croatia
  • Cyprus
  • Czechia
  • Denmark
  • Estonia
  • Finland
  • France
  • Germany
  • Gibraltar
  • Greece
  • Holy See
  • Hungary
  • Iceland
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Latvia
  • Liechtenstein
  • Lithuania
  • Luxembourg
  • Malta
  • Monaco
  • Netherlands
  • Norway
  • Poland
  • Portugal
  • Romania
  • San Marino
  • Slovakia
  • Slovenia
  • Spain
  • Sweden
  • Switzerland

Applicants living in a European overseas territory may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which they are a citizen.

Academic and Professional Requirements

In addition to meeting the standard Chevening eligibility criteria, applicants must meet several fellowship-specific requirements.

Postgraduate Qualification

Applicants must hold a postgraduate qualification, or have equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field.

Professional Experience

Applicants must have at least five years of relevant professional experience.

This makes the fellowship particularly suitable for experienced professionals rather than recent graduates or early-career applicants.

Relevant Professional Sector

Applicants must be mid-career professionals employed within areas such as:

  • Government
  • Defence
  • Security
  • Law enforcement
  • Intelligence
  • Civil protection
  • Resilience
  • International organisations with responsibilities for national or international security

Leadership Potential

Applicants must be able to demonstrate leadership potential.

The fellowship is aimed at professionals who have the potential to contribute to organisational and national security-related priorities through their leadership.

Ability to Influence

Applicants should be working in roles that have the potential to influence:

  • Organisational capability
  • Policy
  • Strategy
  • Operational effectiveness

This influence may be within the applicant’s organisation and/or country.

Commitment After the Fellowship

Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to applying the knowledge, experience, and professional networks gained through the fellowship after completing the programme.

This means applicants should be able to explain how the fellowship could contribute to their future professional work and wider organisational or national impact.

Funding and Benefits

The fellowship provides financial support to successful participants.

According to the provided information, each fellowship includes:

Full Programme Fees

The fellowship covers the full programme fees.

Living Expenses

Fellows receive living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford, as stated in the provided programme information.

Return Economy Airfare

The fellowship also includes return economy airfare.

These provisions are intended to support fellows throughout their participation in the six-week programme.

Why This Fellowship Is Relevant to Today’s Security Environment

Security and defence professionals increasingly need to understand issues beyond traditional security structures.

A contemporary security environment can involve interconnected challenges relating to:

  • Cybersecurity
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Emerging technologies
  • Organisational resilience
  • Governance
  • Human behaviour
  • Leadership
  • Information threats
  • International cooperation
  • Strategic decision-making

The fellowship’s interdisciplinary structure reflects this broader environment.

By bringing these subjects together, the programme aims to help professionals develop a more comprehensive understanding of the challenges faced by modern governments, organisations, and institutions.

Application Deadline

Applications for the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship are open until:

27 September 2026 at 11:00 UTC

Applicants should ensure that their application is submitted before the stated deadline.

Late applications may not be considered, so prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to review the eligibility criteria and prepare their application.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants can apply through the official Chevening application system.

Apply for the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully review both the standard Chevening eligibility requirements and the additional requirements for the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship.

What Makes a Strong Candidate for This Fellowship?

Based on the requirements provided, a strong candidate would be someone who can demonstrate several important characteristics.

1. Relevant Professional Experience

The applicant should have substantial experience in a relevant security, defence, government, resilience, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, or international organisation environment.

2. Leadership Potential

Applicants should demonstrate that they have the potential to become or continue developing as influential leaders within their professional environment.

3. Strategic Responsibilities

The applicant’s current position should provide opportunities to influence policy, strategy, organisational capability, or operational effectiveness.

4. Understanding of Security Challenges

Applicants should be able to demonstrate an understanding of contemporary security and defence challenges relevant to their work.

5. Future Application of Knowledge

Candidates should clearly demonstrate how they intend to apply the knowledge and networks gained during the fellowship after returning to their organisation or country.

Important Information for Applicants

The Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is a specialised programme with specific professional requirements.

It is therefore important for applicants to distinguish between simply having an interest in defence or security and actually meeting the programme’s professional eligibility requirements.

The fellowship specifically targets mid-career professionals whose current employment and responsibilities are connected to security, defence, resilience, government, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, or relevant international organisations.

Applicants should also pay attention to the requirement concerning the ability to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Europe Defence and Security Fellowship?

The Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is a six-week Chevening fellowship funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom in Shrivenham.

How long does the fellowship last?

The fellowship lasts for six weeks.

When are the 2027 cohorts?

There are two cohorts:

  • Cohort 1: 25 January – 5 March 2027
  • Cohort 2: 15 March – 23 April 2027

Who is the fellowship designed for?

It is designed for mid-career professionals from eligible European countries who have demonstrated leadership potential in defence and security.

Do I need a postgraduate qualification?

Yes. Applicants must hold a postgraduate qualification or have equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field.

How much professional experience is required?

Applicants must have at least five years of relevant professional experience.

Can professionals working in law enforcement apply?

Yes. Law enforcement is among the professional sectors specifically identified in the eligibility requirements.

Can intelligence professionals apply?

Yes. Intelligence professionals are included among the eligible professional profiles.

Can government employees apply?

Yes. Government professionals working in relevant security and defence contexts can apply, subject to meeting all other eligibility requirements.

Is the fellowship funded?

Yes. The provided information states that the fellowship includes full programme fees, living expenses including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford, and return economy airfare.

What is the application deadline?

The application deadline is 27 September 2026 at 11:00 UTC.

Is the fellowship open worldwide?

No. The provided eligibility requirements specify citizenship and residency in particular European countries. Applicants must also meet the programme’s professional and academic requirements.

Conclusion

The Europe Defence and Security Fellowship 2027 offers a specialised six-week professional development experience for mid-career European professionals working in defence, security, government, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, and relevant international organisations.

Delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom and funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, the programme combines academic learning with practical exercises, simulations, workshops, institutional visits, research, practitioner engagement, and international networking.

Its six core themes cover global leadership, organisational culture, cyber resilience, artificial intelligence and emerging technology, strategic decision-making, and future leadership and resilience. Fellows will also undertake an individual research project and present their findings to the FCDO in London at the end of the fellowship.

The opportunity is particularly suited to professionals who already have substantial experience and responsibilities within the defence and security environment and who can demonstrate the potential to influence policy, strategy, organisational capability, or operational effectiveness.

Eligible professionals should take note of the 27 September 2026 at 11:00 UTC application deadline and carefully assess the programme’s citizenship, residency, academic, professional, and leadership requirements before submitting an application.

Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026: One-to-One Oxford Application Guidance for African Students

Are you an African student considering applying to the University of Oxford but unsure about where to begin, how the application process works, or what you should do to prepare a competitive application?

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 provides an opportunity for prospective African applicants to receive personalised guidance from people who have direct experience with Oxford. Through the programme, selected mentees will be connected with current Oxford students or Oxford alumni who can share their experiences, answer questions and provide guidance as participants navigate the Oxford application process.

The mentorship programme will run from September to December 2026 and will provide one-to-one mentorship support to African students who are considering applying to the University of Oxford.

Interested applicants are required to complete the programme’s application form by 20 September 2026.

What Is the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme?

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is designed to help prospective African applicants approach the University of Oxford application process with greater confidence.

Applying to Oxford can be a complex process, particularly for students who may not have direct access to someone who has previously studied at Oxford or gone through the university’s application process. Applicants may have questions about where to start, how to prepare, what the experience of applying is like, and how to navigate the various stages involved.

The mentorship programme seeks to bridge that information gap by connecting prospective applicants with individuals who have first-hand experience of Oxford.

Selected participants will receive one-to-one mentorship from a current Oxford student or an Oxford alumnus/alumna. This provides mentees with an opportunity to have conversations with someone who understands the Oxford environment and can share personal experiences and insights.

What Does the Mentorship Programme Offer?

The programme focuses on providing prospective applicants with support as they consider and prepare for an Oxford application.

Through the mentorship relationship, participants can benefit from:

  • One-to-one mentorship support.
  • Guidance from a current Oxford student or Oxford alumnus/alumna.
  • The opportunity to ask questions about applying to Oxford.
  • First-hand perspectives and experiences from people who have studied at Oxford.
  • Support in navigating the application process with greater confidence.
  • An opportunity to gain a better understanding of what the Oxford application journey can involve.
  • Personalised conversations with a mentor matched to the participant.

Rather than simply providing general information, the programme is structured around a mentor-mentee relationship, allowing participants to engage directly with someone who can answer questions and share their own experiences.

Who Can Apply for the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme?

The programme is aimed at African students who are considering applying to the University of Oxford.

It may be particularly valuable for prospective applicants who:

  1. Are African students.
  2. Are considering submitting an application to the University of Oxford.
  3. Want to understand the Oxford application process better.
  4. Would like to speak with someone who has direct experience with Oxford.
  5. Have questions about preparing for an Oxford application.
  6. Would benefit from individual guidance and mentorship.
  7. Want to approach the application process with greater confidence.

The programme is therefore not intended as a general mentorship opportunity for all students. Its specific focus is on African applicants interested in applying to the University of Oxford.

Why Oxford Application Mentorship Can Be Valuable

For prospective applicants, one of the biggest challenges can be knowing where to begin.

Students may find themselves researching Oxford independently and encountering large amounts of information without knowing which aspects are most relevant to their individual circumstances. Speaking directly with someone who has experienced Oxford as a student can provide an additional perspective.

A mentor can offer insight based on their own experience, help a mentee think through questions and provide a clearer understanding of the application journey.

The Afox-AfriSoc programme therefore gives prospective applicants an opportunity to learn from people who have first-hand knowledge of Oxford rather than having to navigate every question alone.

How the Mentorship Programme Works

The programme is scheduled to take place between September and December 2026.

Applicants first need to complete the designated mentorship programme form. Following submission, the organisers will review applications and determine which applicants are accepted onto the programme.

According to the programme information, applicants will be contacted by early October 2026 to be informed about whether they have been accepted.

For applicants who are selected, additional information will then be provided about their mentor match.

The overall process can therefore be understood in the following stages:

1. Complete the Application Form

Interested prospective applicants must complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme form.

The form requests basic personal and contact information, including:

  • First name
  • Surname
  • Email address
  • Nationality
  • Country of residence
  • Gender
  • WhatsApp number

Applicants should ensure that the information they provide is accurate and that their contact details are active.

2. Submit the Form Before the Deadline

The application form must be completed by:

20 September 2026

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day where possible, particularly if they need additional time to review their information before submitting the form.

3. Application Review

After the deadline, applications will be considered by the programme organisers.

The information provided in the form will be used as part of the programme’s selection process.

4. Receive the Selection Outcome

The organisers state that applicants will be contacted by early October 2026 to inform them whether they have been accepted onto the programme.

5. Mentor Matching

Applicants who are accepted will receive further information about their mentor match.

The programme aims to connect mentees with current Oxford students or alumni, creating an opportunity for participants to receive guidance from someone with direct Oxford experience.

6. Participate in the Mentorship Programme

The programme will run from September to December 2026.

During this period, selected mentees will receive one-to-one mentorship support as they navigate questions surrounding their potential Oxford application.

What Kind of Questions Can Prospective Applicants Explore With a Mentor?

The programme description specifically highlights the opportunity for mentors to share their experiences, answer questions and help mentees navigate the application process.

This means prospective applicants can use the mentorship relationship to better understand aspects of the Oxford application journey that they may otherwise find difficult to navigate independently.

Potential areas of discussion could include understanding the overall application journey, learning about a mentor’s personal experience at Oxford, discussing questions about preparing to apply and gaining a better understanding of the university from the perspective of someone who has studied there.

The mentorship should therefore be viewed as an opportunity to learn, ask questions and gain perspective, rather than simply as a formal application service.

Who Will the Mentors Be?

Selected mentees will be matched with either:

  • A current University of Oxford student, or
  • An Oxford alumnus/alumna.

This is one of the central features of the programme.

Instead of receiving guidance exclusively from general admissions resources, participants have the opportunity to interact with someone who has direct experience of Oxford.

A current student may be able to share their experience of being at Oxford at present, while an alumnus or alumna can provide insight based on their own time at the university and application journey.

Important Dates for the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026

Prospective applicants should take note of the following dates:

Application deadline: 20 September 2026

Expected notification: Early October 2026

Mentorship period: September to December 2026

Applicants should make sure that their application form is submitted before the stated deadline.

Information Required on the Application Form

The application form begins by requesting applicants’ personal and contact information.

Applicants are asked to provide:

Personal Information

  • First Name
  • Surname
  • Nationality
  • Country of Residence
  • Gender

The gender options shown on the form are:

  • Male
  • Female
  • Prefer not to say
  • Other

Contact Information

Applicants are also required to provide:

  • E-mail Address
  • WhatsApp Number

The WhatsApp number is particularly important because it may provide the organisers with another way of communicating with participants.

Applicants should therefore provide an active contact number that they regularly monitor.

Why African Students Considering Oxford Should Consider Applying

The programme offers an opportunity for prospective African applicants to access a form of guidance that can be difficult to obtain independently.

Students considering Oxford may have questions that are difficult to answer simply by reading general information online. A conversation with someone who has actually experienced the university can provide a different perspective.

The mentorship programme can potentially help participants:

  • Become more familiar with the Oxford application journey.
  • Ask questions directly to someone with Oxford experience.
  • Learn from the experiences of current students or alumni.
  • Gain confidence while considering an application.
  • Better understand what it may be like to study at Oxford.
  • Think more carefully about their application preparation.
  • Access individual rather than purely general guidance.

For students who are serious about exploring an Oxford application, having access to a mentor can therefore be a valuable addition to their preparation.

Application Deadline

The deadline to complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 form is:

APPLY HERE.

20 September 2026

Prospective mentees should ensure that their forms are completed and submitted by this date.

Because the programme organisers indicate that they will communicate the outcome by early October, applicants should also ensure that the email address and WhatsApp number they provide remain accessible after submitting the form.

When Will Applicants Hear Back?

According to the information provided by the programme organisers, applicants will receive an update by early October 2026.

The update will inform applicants whether they have been accepted onto the mentorship programme.

Those who are accepted will receive additional information regarding their mentor match.

Mentorship Period

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is scheduled to run from:

September to December 2026

This gives selected participants several months during which they can receive mentorship and engage with their matched Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.

The programme is therefore intended to provide ongoing support rather than a single information session.

What Applicants Should Do Before Applying

Prospective mentees should take the opportunity to think carefully about why they are interested in Oxford and what they hope to gain from mentorship.

Before submitting the form, applicants can consider:

  1. Why they are interested in applying to Oxford.
  2. What questions they have about the application process.
  3. What areas they would like guidance on.
  4. What they hope to learn from an Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.
  5. Whether their contact details are correct and active.
  6. Whether they can participate during the September-to-December 2026 mentorship period.

Having clear questions and goals can help a mentee make better use of a mentorship opportunity if selected.

For more information, CLICK HERE.

Is This a Scholarship?

No.

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is not described as a scholarship. The information provided describes it as a mentorship programme designed to connect prospective African Oxford applicants with current Oxford students and alumni.

There is no information in the provided announcement indicating that the programme provides tuition funding, living expenses, application fee funding or a scholarship award.

Students should therefore understand this opportunity primarily as an application guidance and mentorship programme.

Is This an Oxford Admission Programme?

The mentorship programme should also not be confused with an official Oxford admissions offer or an admissions decision.

Participation in mentorship does not mean that a student has been admitted to the University of Oxford.

Instead, the purpose of the programme is to support prospective applicants as they consider and navigate the application process.

Students who participate should still follow the official University of Oxford admissions requirements and deadlines relevant to the course or programme they eventually choose to apply for.

Key Details at a Glance

Programme: Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme

Opportunity type: Mentorship programme

Target participants: African students considering applying to the University of Oxford

Mentor: Current Oxford student or Oxford alumnus/alumna

Format: One-to-one mentorship

Programme period: September to December 2026

Application deadline: 20 September 2026

Expected selection notification: Early October 2026

Purpose: To help prospective African Oxford applicants gain guidance, ask questions, learn from Oxford experiences and navigate the application process with greater confidence.

How to Apply

Interested African students should complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme application form provided by the organisers.

Applicants should carefully provide the requested personal and contact information and submit the completed form before the deadline of 20 September 2026.

Because the programme organisers indicate that successful applicants will receive further information about their mentor match, applicants should monitor the email address and contact information provided on their application after submission.

Final Thoughts

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 provides prospective African applicants to the University of Oxford with an opportunity to receive individual guidance from people who have direct experience of the university.

For students who are interested in Oxford but are uncertain about how to begin, the programme can provide an important opportunity to ask questions, learn from current students or alumni and approach the application process with greater confidence.

The programme will run from September to December 2026, with accepted participants receiving one-to-one mentorship from a current Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.

African students considering an Oxford application should take note of the 20 September 2026 application deadline and complete the mentorship programme form before the closing date.

For prospective applicants, this could be an opportunity to gain valuable insight and personalised support while preparing to take the next step towards an Oxford application.

For more OFY Mentorship opportunities, visit HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants Program 2027 is now open for applications from eligible Chicago-based organizations working to improve opportunities and outcomes for young people.

Through the 2027 grant cycle, McDonald’s is committing an additional $4 million to support local nonprofit organizations addressing two important challenges affecting young people in underserved Chicago communities: workforce readiness and development and food access and insecurity.

Selected organizations can receive project-based grants ranging from $50,000 to $200,000, with up to 25 grants expected to be awarded. The initiative is designed to support programs that create measurable improvements in the lives of young people between the ages of 16 and 24.

Applications opened on September 1, 2026, and the application deadline is September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Central Time (CT).

Overview of the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants 2027

McDonald’s has a longstanding connection to Chicago, where the company is headquartered. Through its community investment efforts, the company supports programs intended to strengthen communities, expand access to opportunity and address pressing local challenges.

The Chicago Community Impact Grants Program was launched in 2022 in partnership with The Chicago Community Trust. Since its launch, McDonald’s reports that it has invested more than $12 million in support of local organizations and reached more than 100,000 people across Chicago.

For the 2027 cycle, McDonald’s is providing an additional $4 million to continue supporting organizations that are creating meaningful change in Chicago.

The 2027 initiative places particular emphasis on empowering young people and helping them overcome barriers that can prevent them from accessing education, employment, economic opportunity and adequate food.

The program is organized around two major priorities:

  1. Fostering Communities: Pathways to Empowerment
  2. Feeding Futures: Food Access and Insecurity

Organizations applying for funding should ensure that their proposed project clearly aligns with at least one of these priority areas.

1. Fostering Communities: Pathways to Empowerment

The first priority area focuses on workforce readiness and development for youth ages 16–24.

McDonald’s recognizes that young people do not all follow the same pathway to employment and economic success. Some face significant barriers involving transportation, financial knowledge, access to professional networks, mentorship, training and exposure to potential careers.

Through the Fostering Communities priority, the grant program seeks to support organizations implementing programs that take a holistic approach to removing these barriers.

The goal is not simply to provide young people with short-term activities. Rather, supported programs should help participants develop the knowledge, skills, experience and support systems they need to move toward meaningful employment and long-term economic opportunity.

What types of workforce programs can be funded?

Eligible organizations may request funding for direct workforce-readiness services and initiatives such as:

  • Apprenticeships that provide young people with practical, hands-on work experience.
  • Pre-employment training designed to prepare participants for entering the workforce.
  • Post-employment training that helps young workers strengthen their skills and succeed after securing employment.
  • Career exposure opportunities that introduce young people to different industries, occupations, professional environments and career pathways.
  • Other workforce development activities that directly contribute to improving employment readiness and access to opportunity.

The emphasis is on programs that provide practical benefits and can demonstrate meaningful outcomes for young participants.

Holistic support services

The program also recognizes that workforce participation can be affected by challenges outside the classroom or workplace.

Consequently, applicants may include funding requests for holistic support services that directly strengthen their core workforce programming.

Examples include:

Transportation and mobility assistance

Transportation can be a significant barrier for young people attempting to participate in training, apprenticeships, interviews, internships or employment.

Organizations may therefore incorporate transportation or mobility support where it directly contributes to successful participation in their workforce programs.

Financial literacy education

Financial literacy can help young people better understand budgeting, saving, responsible financial decision-making and other issues associated with economic independence.

Programs may incorporate financial literacy when it directly supports their broader workforce-readiness objectives.

Mentorship and coaching

Mentorship and coaching can provide participants with guidance, encouragement, professional insight and accountability as they navigate education, training and employment pathways.

Applicants can therefore include appropriate mentoring and coaching components as part of a broader workforce development program.

The key consideration is that these support services should directly enhance the organization’s core workforce programming, rather than operate as unrelated activities.

2. Feeding Futures: Food Access and Insecurity

The second priority area focuses on food access and food insecurity among youth ages 16–24 in underserved communities.

As a global food company, McDonald’s states that it seeks to play a positive role in the communities it serves, including through initiatives that improve access to food.

The Feeding Futures priority is intended to support organizations developing practical responses to food insecurity and barriers to accessing food.

Programs can focus on providing direct food assistance, expanding local food production, improving access to food in underserved neighborhoods or developing community-led approaches to addressing systemic barriers.

Examples of eligible food-access initiatives

Funding may support programs such as:

  • Food banks and food pantries that provide consistent access to nutritious food and meals.
  • Community gardens that promote local food production and community participation.
  • Urban farms that expand local food production and improve food availability.
  • Mobile markets that bring food to neighborhoods experiencing limited access to grocery stores and other food sources.
  • Community-led solutions designed to remove systemic barriers to food access.
  • Other direct services and initiatives that align with the program’s food access and food insecurity objectives for young people ages 16–24.

Organizations should demonstrate how their proposed project addresses an identifiable food-access challenge and how young people in underserved Chicago communities will benefit.

Who Should Apply for the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants?

The program is designed for Chicago-based organizations serving young people ages 16–24 through programs aligned with one of the two priority areas.

Applicants should not simply demonstrate that they work with young people. Their proposed project must have a clear connection to either:

  • Workforce readiness and development; or
  • Food access and food insecurity.

Organizations should also be able to demonstrate that they have the experience, systems and financial capacity necessary to responsibly manage grant funding and implement the proposed project.

Grant Eligibility and Selection Criteria

McDonald’s has established several criteria that applicants must satisfy.

1. Serve youth ages 16–24

Applicants must operate programs serving young people between the ages of 16 and 24.

The proposed program should clearly demonstrate how it will benefit this population and how it aligns with one of the two focus areas.

2. Demonstrate measurable impact

Applicants should have a track record of delivering programs that produce meaningful outcomes.

Organizations should be able to demonstrate evidence of:

  • Successful program delivery.
  • Positive outcomes for participants.
  • Measurable community impact.
  • Effective engagement with the communities they serve.

A strong application should therefore go beyond describing activities and explain what changes the organization has achieved or expects to achieve.

3. Demonstrate organizational and financial capacity

Organizations must have the organizational and financial systems necessary to successfully implement and manage the proposed project.

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate responsible stewardship of resources and the ability to administer grant funding effectively.

4. Maintain strong community relationships

Applicants should have established relationships within the communities they serve.

McDonald’s is looking for organizations with credibility and a reputation for:

  • Responsible stewardship.
  • Integrity.
  • Community service.
  • Meaningful community engagement.
  • Positive relationships with the populations they serve.

How McDonald’s Will Evaluate Applications

This is a competitive grantmaking process. Submitting an application does not guarantee funding.

Eligible applications will be reviewed, evaluated and scored using the program’s published criteria.

Several major factors will influence the assessment.

Financial Health

McDonald’s will consider the organization’s:

  • Financial stability.
  • Stewardship of resources.
  • Funding diversity.
  • Ability to sustain its operations.
  • Capacity to effectively implement the proposed program.

Applicants should therefore present a credible picture of their financial health and demonstrate that they can responsibly manage the proposed grant.

Program Alignment

The proposed project must demonstrate strong alignment with one of the two 2027 priorities:

  • Feeding Futures: Food Access and Insecurity, or
  • Fostering Communities: Pathways to Empowerment.

A proposal that does not clearly connect its activities and intended outcomes to these priorities is likely to be less competitive.

Impact

McDonald’s will assess the organization’s ability to demonstrate meaningful and measurable outcomes.

Applicants should clearly explain:

  • Who will benefit.
  • What problem the project addresses.
  • What activities will be implemented.
  • How many people are expected to benefit.
  • What outcomes are expected.
  • How progress and success will be measured.

Organizational Brand and Reputational Risk

McDonald’s will also consider an organization’s credibility, community reputation and alignment with its values and community-impact priorities.

This means applicants should demonstrate that they are trusted organizations with a responsible approach to serving their communities.

How Much Funding Is Available?

The 2027 Chicago Community Impact Grants Program will provide $4 million in additional funding.

Individual grant awards will range from:

  • Minimum grant: $50,000
  • Maximum grant: $200,000

The final amount awarded to each organization will depend on the strength of its application and its alignment with the goals of the Chicago Community Impact Grants Program.

McDonald’s expects to award up to 25 grants.

Importantly, this is a competitive process. Being eligible does not mean an organization will automatically receive funding.

Funding decisions will take into consideration factors including:

  • Alignment with the program’s focus areas.
  • Expected community impact.
  • Financial health.
  • Organizational capacity.
  • Geographic focus.
  • Community credibility.
  • Overall application strength.
  • The strength and feasibility of the proposed project.

What Makes an Application Competitive?

Because funding is competitive, organizations should avoid treating the application as simply a request for financial assistance.

A strong application should demonstrate a clear connection between the organization’s existing work, the proposed project and the objectives of the grant program.

Applicants should consider emphasizing the following areas.

Clearly define the problem

Explain the specific challenge affecting youth ages 16–24 in the Chicago community being served.

For a workforce proposal, this could involve barriers to employment, limited career exposure, inadequate job-readiness skills or other obstacles to opportunity.

For a food-access proposal, the organization should clearly explain the food insecurity or food-access challenge affecting the target population.

Demonstrate evidence of impact

Provide concrete evidence of previous results wherever possible.

Organizations should demonstrate that they have experience implementing effective programs and achieving measurable outcomes.

Connect every activity to the priority area

The proposed activities should have a direct relationship to either workforce development or food access.

Avoid including activities simply because they are generally beneficial to young people. The proposal should explain why each major activity is necessary to achieve the project’s intended outcomes.

Present a realistic implementation plan

Explain how the organization will use the grant to implement the project.

The proposal should demonstrate that the organization has the people, partnerships, systems and experience required to execute the program successfully.

Demonstrate financial responsibility

Since financial health and stewardship are part of the evaluation process, organizations should ensure that their financial information and proposed use of funds are clear, credible and responsible.

Important Application Dates for the 2027 Grant Cycle

Organizations interested in the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants Program should pay close attention to the following dates:

Important date Details
September 1, 2026 Applications open
September 10, 2026 Informational Webinar
September 30, 2026 Application deadline
11:59 PM CT Application closing time

Application deadline

The final deadline to apply is September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Central Time (CT).

Organizations should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Applicants should allow sufficient time to review their responses, confirm supporting information and ensure the application is successfully submitted before the deadline.

McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants Informational Webinar

McDonald’s will host an Informational Webinar on September 10, 2026 to provide additional information and help interested organizations prepare their applications.

Organizations considering applying are encouraged to participate in the webinar to better understand the grant opportunity and application process.

Prospective applicants should use the webinar as the primary source of additional clarification because McDonald’s states that, in order to maintain a fair application process, the Community Impact Team will not conduct preliminary or informational calls with prospective applicants.

How to Apply for the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants 2027

Eligible organizations can submit their applications through the official application platform.

Application: Apply for the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants 2027

Before submitting, organizations should carefully review the grant priorities and ensure that their proposed project fits within either the workforce-readiness or food-access focus.

Applicants should also ensure that their organization can demonstrate the required program experience, measurable impact, organizational capacity, financial health and community credibility.

Questions About the Grant Program

Applicants who have questions should consult the official McDonald’s grant resources and informational webinar.

The program provides a designated Community Impact Team email for questions:

community@mcd.com

However, applicants should note that McDonald’s has stated that it will not conduct preliminary or informational calls with prospective applicants. This is intended to maintain a fair application process for all organizations.

Why This Grant Opportunity Matters for Chicago Nonprofits

The McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants Program represents a significant funding opportunity for nonprofit organizations working directly with young people in Chicago.

The $50,000–$200,000 grant range can provide substantial project-based support for organizations that already have the infrastructure and community relationships needed to deliver effective programs.

The two priority areas also address major issues that can have long-term consequences for young people.

Workforce readiness can help young people develop skills, gain practical experience, explore career pathways and overcome barriers to employment.

Food-access initiatives can help address immediate food insecurity while also supporting longer-term community solutions such as urban agriculture, community gardens, mobile markets and community-led food systems.

By focusing specifically on youth ages 16–24, the program seeks to support young people during an important period of education, workforce entry and transition toward greater economic independence.

Key Facts About the McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants 2027

  • Program: McDonald’s Chicago Community Impact Grants Program 2027
  • Funder: McDonald’s
  • Community partner: The Chicago Community Trust
  • Total additional funding: $4 million
